idiom_name: one context struct threaded as a pointer; C11 _Thread_local only for thread-bound infrastructure
implementation_notes: C has no components and no ambient scope, so the relay is a pointer argument on every function between owner and consumer (`int render_page(struct app_ctx *ctx, ...)`), and the smell looks the same as in UI code: a function grows a `ctx` parameter it only forwards. What replaces the classic structure is grouping and discipline - keep the relayed values in one small, const-correct context struct and pass that pointer instead of five scalars, and keep the pointer only on paths that actually read part of it. `_Thread_local` (C11) plus a file-scope accessor is the only ambient mechanism the language offers; it trades traceability for convenience and belongs to thread-bound infrastructure (allocators, error state), never to request data that should stay visible in signatures.
pitfalls: `_Thread_local` state is per thread: a pool that reuses threads leaks one request's values into the next unless every entry point resets it.
A context struct passed as a non-const pointer invites intermediates to mutate shared members; keep relayed fields const or the value changes behind the owner's back.
Every signature on the path changes when the context gains a field, and nothing in the compiler warns about a forwarded-but-unused parameter - the smell is invisible to the toolchain.
